solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Remaining? No more!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: left ..., as in food still uneaten
second meaning: finished, as when a game has ended

explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation makes it look like a question and a reply at the table; the two halves are separate senses of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both left behind unused and finished completely, so it fits each half of the clue.

clue.text: Painter very excited about new hotel

parts.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very

indicators.note: about means around, so the next piece sits inside the excited one

parts.note: agog means eagerly excited
N is the abbreviation for new
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An artist is thrilled by the opening of a new hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincent van Gogh was the Dutch Post-Impressionist painter of Sunflowers and The Starry Night.

clue.text: Uplifting beverage fit for the Queen

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: lager is a beer, one kind of beverage

explanation.surface: A cheering drink worthy of serving to royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' looks like praise for the drink; in a down answer it turns the word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means royal, befitting a king or queen, so something fit for the monarch.

clue.text: Live tennis shot in advance

parts.note: to live is to exist, to be
a stroke played palm-forward in tennis

explanation.surface: A sports fan wants to book a live tennis match ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' reads as an adjective for a broadcast, but it is the verb meaning to exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done ahead of time, before the event, is done in advance; the two expressions are synonyms.

clue.text: Uncivilised nature of pub is shown in yeasty froth on liquor

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: something shown in a frame sits within it, so it goes inside

parts.note: barm is the froth on fermenting malt liquor
taken as written

explanation.surface: The rough character of a pub is revealed in the foam on its beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Barm is the yeasty froth skimmed from brewing, the source of the word barmy.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarism is the state of being uncivilised, savage or crude in behaviour or condition.

clue.text: Worried about fine jewellery losing its centrepiece

indicators.note: losing a centrepiece means the letter in the very middle is removed

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an earring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a delicate piece of jewellery whose central stone has fallen out.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the middle R of the seven-letter EARRING leaves EARING.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fearing something is to be anxious over it, which is what worried about means as a participle.

clue.text: Stacks of wrenches

definitions.meaning: first meaning: haystacks built in a field
second meaning: sprains or twists of a joint

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a pile of spanners; 'wrenches' is the verb or noun for straining a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names piles of hay or straw and also sprains, as when someone twists their neck.

clue.text: God alters intro to "Oi!" in greeting commoners

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next piece
altering an intro means the opening letter is swapped for something else

parts.note: an informal hello
the Greek god of the sun and music
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deity shouts a rough 'Oi!' instead of a polite hello to ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the god's opening letter is replaced, by both letters of the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi is a Greek phrase for the many, used in English for the masses or ordinary people.

clue.text: Twelve having bother getting in shape

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: twelve o'clock midday
to nag is to pester or bother

explanation.surface: Twelve people struggle to get into shape at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twelve' suggests a number of sides, a tempting false lead for a shape; it is the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a polygon with nine sides, so it is a particular geometric figure.

clue.text: Men fed horse first to enrage another equid

indicators.note: when one thing is fed something, that something goes inside it

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers who are not officers
a nag is an old or poor horse

indicators.note: the first of a word means only its opening letter is wanted

parts.note: opening letter of enrage

explanation.surface: Soldiers feed a horse first, which annoys a different animal waiting its turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enrage' tempts an anagram, but only its first letter is used; 'first' attaches to it, not to the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An onager is a wild ass of Asia, so like the horse in the clue it is a member of the equid family.

clue.text: Sales for everyone wearing suits

indicators.note: something worn sits inside clothing, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: lawsuits are legal actions
U is the British film certificate meaning universal, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A shop advertises sales where everyone shows up in business suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suits' looks like clothing, which fits 'wearing', but here they are court cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Auctions are public sales where goods go to the highest bidder, a particular kind of sale.

clue.text: Short bloke with hair styled something like a cabbage

indicators.note: hair that is styled is rearranged, so these letters are rearranged too
something cut short is missing its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A short man has his hair styled into something resembling a cabbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohlrabi is a vegetable of the cabbage family with a swollen edible stem, so it is literally cabbage-like.

clue.text: Discard top of swimsuit? See, that's disgusting!

indicators.note: the top of a down-reading word is its first letter

parts.note: opening letter of swimsuit
lo is an old word meaning look or see
an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone is told to remove the top half of a swimsuit and reacts with disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: To slough is to shed or cast off, as a snake does with its skin, so it means to throw away.

clue.text: Keeping Status Quo waiting on the phone

definitions.meaning: first meaning: refusing to change position or give ground
second meaning: staying connected on a call while waiting

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make you picture the rock band Status Quo kept on hold; the phrase is simply the status quo, things as they are.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means resisting change and also, literally, staying on a telephone call while waiting.

clue.text: Puppies annoy one leaving droppings

parts.note: a litter is a set of young born together
to bug is to irritate

explanation.surface: Puppies are a nuisance because they leave messes everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Droppings' suggests animal mess, but it means rubbish dropped in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug is a person who carelessly drops rubbish in public places, leaving it behind.

clue.text: Suffering? Try toothbrush, perhaps?

parts.note: a judge tries or hears a case
a toothbrush is a short, square style of moustache

explanation.surface: Advice for someone in pain: maybe brushing teeth will help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toothbrush' suggests dentistry, but it is a type of clipped moustache; tache is British slang for a moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional suffering or anguish, deep sorrow felt over a loss or disappointment.

clue.text: Damaged enamel? It's mints being too sweet

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so the letters following are broken and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dentist blames tooth decay on eating too many sweet mints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too sweet' seems to describe the mints, but it is the definition in its figurative sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentimentalism is excessive, mawkish feeling, so being cloying or syrupy in emotion rather than in taste.

clue.text: Obvious occasion to carry a passport?

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: an event is an occasion
a passport is a form of identification

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders whether this is clearly an occasion to bring a passport.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a passport is just one example of ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plainly seen or clear to the eye or mind, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Nut in case most generous

parts.note: nut and nob are both slang for the head
lest means for fear that, in case

explanation.surface: A nut in its shell turns out to be the most bountiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' and 'case' suggest a shell, but nut is slang for the head, as is nob.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble can mean magnanimous or high-minded in character, so the superlative is the most giving.

clue.text: Maureen's in Alsace, she makes wine …

parts.note: Mo is a short form of Maureen, with the apostrophe s kept
the French word for she, as spoken in Alsace

explanation.surface: A woman named Maureen, living in Alsace, is a winemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Alsace is a French region, so 'she' there is the French pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is a white wine from the Moselle valley of Germany and France, named after the river.

clue.text: Several footballers going to the ground, needlessly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old word for various or sundry

definitions.text: footballers going to the ground, needlessly
definitions.meaning: second meaning: players who fall over to win a foul

explanation.walkthrough: In football a diver is a player who falls theatrically to win a free kick; the archaic adjective means various.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old adjective for various or sundry, and also the plural of a player who fakes being fouled.

clue.text: … but without love for wine

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: but and save both mean except
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: she makes wine, but without love.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue's story. 'Without' looks like lacking, but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white Italian wine from the Veneto, named after its home town.

clue.text: Yet to lock in support for Notre Dame?

parts.note: yet and but both mean however
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone has yet to fasten up support for a famous Paris cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: Notre Dame is famous for its flying buttresses.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttress is a projecting structure that props up a wall, as on Gothic cathedrals like Notre Dame.

clue.text: Approval to demolish the front and rear

indicators.note: knocking down the front of a building removes its opening letter

parts.note: praise is warm approval

explanation.surface: Planners approve demolishing a building's front and back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear' looks like the back of the building, matching 'front'; it is the verb meaning to bring up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children or animals is to bring them up, and to raise them is the same, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Mixed veg and Brie covering a waffle

indicators.note: one thing covering another wraps around it, so it goes outside
ingredients that are mixed are jumbled together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe: mixed vegetables and Brie are spread over a waffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waffle' looks like the food, matching the ingredients, but it is the verbal kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbiage is wordy, empty speech or writing, which is exactly what talking waffle means.

clue.text: Country houses start to confiscate gum

indicators.note: a building houses its occupants, holding them inside

parts.note: the South American nation

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: opening letter of confiscate

explanation.surface: Customs officials in some country begin seizing chewing gum.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicle is the natural latex from the sapodilla tree, the traditional base of chewing gum.

clue.text: Six-footer women not allowed to scamper

parts.note: a stag party or night is for men only
to beetle is to scurry along quickly

explanation.surface: A very tall man is told women are not allowed and must hurry off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it is an insect with six legs. A stag do is the British name for a groom's all-male party.
explanation.definitionFit: Every insect has six legs, and this large beetle with antler-like jaws is one such creature.

clue.text: The first habitat lacked enough fences

indicators.note: a fence encloses ground, so the words enclose the letters wanted

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: The earliest settlement did not have adequate fencing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the Garden of Eden is where Adam and Eve, the first humans, lived, so it was the original home.
